item.description: Sudan’s RSF leader, Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, better known as Hemedti, has been handed a second death sentence. A court in Port Sudan has sentenced Hemedti, his two brothers, and 11 others to death by hanging, in absentia, over the looting of Sudan’s medical supplies fund.

item.title: BBC Africa: US consortium wins huge Kenya mining deal, beating Chinese rivals
item.description: The Mrima Hill site is estimated to hold deposits of critical minerals worth more than $60bn (£45bn).

item.title: Africanews: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya, ICJ finds
item.description: Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, the International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday. The landmark judgement marks the first time the Hague-based court has found a state guilty of the crime.

item.title: Africanews: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic trilateral talks on global security
item.description: The trilateral meeting followed separate talks between Trump and Xi, and Trump and Putin. However, analysts remain cautious about the prospects of major breakthroughs given the deep divisions between the three powers.

item.title: BBC Africa: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?
item.description: The Lobito Corridor is at the centre of a US-backed effort to secure access to Africa's critical minerals.

item.title: Africanews: Study finds Islam on track to replace Christianity as biggest religion
item.description: The Pew Research Centre projects both groups will see their numbers increase over the next few decades, but the Muslim population will grow faster.

item.title: BBC Africa: 'It's a dream come true' – South African DJ celebrates featuring in GTA 6
item.description: Several African stars feature

item.title: Africanews: Democrat Hakeem Jeffries on track to become first Black US House speaker
item.description: The secret ballot saw him secure 251 to 11 of the votes to represent the party for the important post at the election in January.

item.title: BBC Africa: World marathon champion Jepchirchir gets three-year doping ban
item.description: Reigning world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir is banned for three years for a doping violation.

item.title: Africanews: Egypt secures $2.3 Billion IMF deal as economic recovery gains momentum
item.description: The agreement comes as Egypt shows signs of economic recovery, with GDP growth reaching 5.1 percent in the 2025–2026 fiscal year, supported by stronger activity in tourism, manufacturing and the Suez Canal.

item.title: BBC Africa: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN
item.description: Survivors reject relocation plans they say ignore their safety, land rights and livelihoods

item.title: Africanews: South Africa orders inquiry into treatment of Olympic swimming champion
item.description: Two-time gold medallist Tatjana Smith last week said she could no longer represent the country bcause of financial challenges.

item.title: Africanews: Trump holds one-on-ones with Putin and Xi ahead of trilateral discussions
item.description: The three powerful men are expected to discuss the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions, and developments in artificial intelligence.

item.title: Africanews: China: Trump calls Putin his "friend" as leaders meet amid in Shenzhen
item.description: Donald Trump greeted Vladimir Putin as his friend during a meeting in Shenzhen. Their 40-minute encounter came ahead of trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

item.title: Africanews: Ukraine: Four killed and at least 13 injured in Russian strike on Odesa
item.description: Russian strikes on the historic centre of Odesa, Ukraine, killed four people and injured at least 13 others on Wednesday 18 November 2026, according to the city’s military administration.

item.title: BBC Africa: Dozens missing after boat carrying 100 migrants sinks off Senegal
item.description: Some local media report that at least four bodies have been recovered.

item.title: BBC Africa: BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa
item.description: The new show brings English, maths and science lessons to children via TV, radio and social media.

item.title: Africanews: Record number of African migrants arrive in Spain's Canary Islands
item.description: Official figures show that more than 11,000 people managed to reach the archipelago in the first 15 days of November, putting pressure on reception facilities.

item.title: Africanews: France: Hundreds raise a glass to Beaujolais Nouveau in Lyon
item.description: Lyon welcomed the arrival of Beaujolais Nouveau with a lively nighttime parade of wine barrels, flaming torches and brass music. Hundreds gathered to celebrate the first tastings of this year's wine.

item.title: Africanews: At least one dead in latest migrant boat disaster off Senegal's coast
item.description: Officials say the wooden vessel carrying around 100 people struck a rocky outcrop and washed ashore overnight Tuesday to Wednesday.

item.title: Africanews: China: Xi, Trump and Putin gather ahead of trilateral summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared together in Shenzhen, on Thursday 19 November 2026, posing for a group photograph alongside other world leaders ahead of a closely watched trilateral summit.

item.title: Africanews: GTA VI launch sparks celebrations in Miami and Dublin
item.description: After 13 years of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived. Fans celebrated at a launch party in Dublin, while Miami Heat supporters rushed to buy limited-edition Vice City merchandise.

item.title: BBC Africa: Divide and conquer - now maverick Erasmus plans online watchalong
item.description: Rassie Erasmus is a serial offender when it comes to criticising officials, but he retains huge support in South Africa - and has unique plans for following his team's game against Ireland.

item.title: BBC Africa: Senegal and Morocco lead Afcon qualifiers but Tunisia protest
item.description: Senegal, Cameroon and Morocco qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, but Nigeria are in trouble, and struggling Tunisia fail with an impassioned penalty protest.

item.title: Africanews: Tunisia olive oil exports jump nearly 50% on bumper harvest
item.description: Tunisia's olive oil exports rose nearly 50%, official figures showed on Wednesday, after a bumper harvest that made it the world's second biggest producer after Spain.
